prompt: In the 23rd century, the United States elects its first Amish president.
story:
"I don't care what you said, get that blasted thing out of here!" I had principles. The people had spoken. Yes, I'd started small. Working my way up meeting by meeting, my competitors had used social media, cameras, online news articles. It was all too impersonal to me. I quite liked the fireside chat style. "If you don't get that camera out of here I'm going to have your job... yes all of them!"

"But Mr. President --" The suited man protested.

"I am the Commander and Chief of this country, my security team will get along just fine without doo-dads and gadgets." I smiled at their horror. I would no doubt change their perspective forever. "We also need candles restocked, a big house like this needs to stay lit."

"But sir, think of the fire hazard." Another protested.

"I am your president, I needn't think of such things. If there is a fire, put it out. I hired you for some reason, though some days you make me wonder..." I shrugged. They would no doubt simplify their lives before the end of my presidency. They elected me for my principles, my unwavering commitment to the tried and true method. No, I never ran under the slogan of "Change", or "Gun Laws", or "Immigration Policies", just the things that work. Like hard work.

"It wasn't until 1891 that this big white building got electricity," I remarked looking pointedly at one of the men on my detail, in his right hand was a glowing box. A touch screen, beeping, buzzing annoyance. "I think you can make it the next 12 hours of your shift without updating the Facebook." I said staring at him. He sheepishly put his phone away.

"I have a meeting tomorrow morning with the ambassador for China, I want no interruptions." I swung open the door to my office, oval. What an odd architectural choice. "I especially want no phone calls. By the end of the month I want all of those off site. Every time one of those damned things goes off I can't sleep. I can't live in a house with possessed objects. I can't, and I won't."

The six men that stood around the oval room looked at each other silently as if to say'What the hell did we get ourselves into?'

prompt: New Horizon speeds past Pluto and into the abyss of unexplored space. Very suddenly, the craft collides into the dome barrier that keeps humanity isolated from the rest of the universe.
story:
Sarah sat, lounging with her son John. They had just finished their evening meal and the 6pm news was on. Sarah liked nights like this. Peaceful. Alone. Just them.

She was not happy with all the reports of the outsiders coming into her country. Silly folks.

As she dwelt on her thoughts of singular disdain for all things not her, the newscasters face turned to one of shock. Not the usual calm demeanor. Not a face that said "trust me," rather one that said "Well. This is it. We're all going to die."

The face then said aloud, "We are getting reports in from NASA that the New Horizons ship has encountered some form of barrier. Something preventing it from moving forth into the galaxy. Wait....."

The voice sounded more and more panicked. Much like a man would if he had a large python moving up his leg and a mouse was taped to his Johnson.

"We are getting reports of a broadcast coming from the ship itse..."

The screen went blank. Flickered. Then a large green face appeared on the screen. Then the screen on her computer. Her phone. Everything. The face was not human. It spoke. It spoke English? Rather proper English too. Unfortunately with a slight Scottish accent.

"Citizens of what you now call'Earth.' We did warn you against this, didn't we? You thought you could stay there. You promised the President himself that you wouldn't. I hope you know..."

The Green face took a deep breath and yelled.

"THAT RESISTANCE IS USELESS"

The Green face looked very happy with itself.

"You need to know that a large Vogon Destructor Fleet is waiting just outside your solar system awaiting orders. The last citizens of Krikkit were given their last chance on Earth 4. You promised that you would not leave the system in any form, on punishment of total destruction."

The face looked somewhat shocked.

"Of course you know what I'm talking about. Silly bloody planet. No Sympathy here. I have to make a living too you know?"

The screens went dark.

Sarah smiled. All the knowledge of a few billion years captivity came flooding into her mind.

She stood up and looked at John, who had picked up his bat and was strapping on his pads.

"The universe. It'll have to go. For good this time."

prompt: 2037, Earth, the human race has come together. The first problem we decide to tackle is the overpopulation of Earth. We must cut our weight by 2/3. With one year to organize and decide who will stay and who will... go. Some will volunteer, some may be forced, this is your story...
story:
*Crack*, the policeman dropped to the floor. Dropping back behind the couch and crawling my way over to the next room, I knew her partner was somewhere in the house. Pulling back the bolt and loading another bullet into the chamber, I crept before freezing. Footsteps, light but close. Jumping to my feet I swung the stock of my rifle as hard as I could, missing and putting a hold in the wall. Pulling his trigger wildly, the officer sent four bullets whizzing behind me, one hitting me in the shoulder. Pivoting my feet, I smashed my shoulder into his jaw through the barrage, forcing him to send what was left of his magazine into the ceiling. I still had four left.

My home was in shambles. I'd gutted all of my electronics following Australia's announcement of compliance, stopped attending university and thrown all my savings into the smuggled rifle and black-market ammunition. I was never particularly strong, intelligent or had any real skills. I was a paragraph monkey. Working freelance alongside my shitty job to make ends meet. Not that it mattered now of course. Kicking out my window after stripping the dead officers in my house of their gear, my car was only a few feet away. Equally shitty as my house, it'd get me where I needed to go. Assuming the coppers didn't send more of course.

Hurling water and food, as well as the surplus of ammo I'd acquired into the boot alongside my spare fuel canisters, I pulled out an expansive map. The route was already planned. Heading northwest west into South Australia I could follow the A87 all the way up to the A1 and to Darwin. Glancing over the edge of the map, I saw the Robinson family being dragged at gunpoint out of their home. Pretty soon, the government had said it would turn back the boats, not that it'd send its own refugees out.

'Time to go.' Sliding my rifle in front of the passenger seat, I left in the confusion. The screams of neighbours ringing in my ears and jaw clenched, I just left. My heart told me I was a coward, but I knew better. As the adrenaline faded, my arm burst into agony, not to mention the bleeding. But it could wait, it could all wait. And if I was lucky, so would any remaining people smugglers.
